- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent prices are rising — model tends to lag or overshoot upward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.1) or flat — model often fails to capture downward momentum or mean reversion.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes: if price spiked recently, model often forecasts a continued rise, but true outcome tends to correct or flatten.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently holds prices too high after a spike, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early 2025 (post-2024) when sentiment is bullish — model overweights sentiment, underweights volatility.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to smooth too much — underestimates sharp reversals or overestimates gradual trends.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should not over-forecast 30-day peak — true outcome often peaks earlier and then declines.
